issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Cosmos-Dreams rollout-owned prefix K/V buffer
issues.body:
## Motivation

Every denoise step, each layer concatenated `[text | history]` and then `[prefix | chunk]`, and every commit re-allocated the whole history. That is 2 full K/V history copies per layer per step plus an O(T) copy per commit.

## Changes

- `PrefixKVHistory` (cosmos_dreams.py): per-layer `[text | history | chunk scratch]` buffers owned by the rollout. Indexing returns history views, so it works anywhere a `list[KVPair]` history is read.
- The transformer writes the chunk's K/V into the scratch rows and attends to a view, so no history copy per step. `_joint_attention` takes `chunk_in_prefix` and keeps its old signature.
- `append_kv_history` appends in place for the buffer, with the same sink + window eviction and the same window check.
- Rollout creates the buffer at the first commit. Its initial capacity is `sink + window + chunk` frames, capped at the request's latent frame count so short requests do not over-reserve. The buffer grows on demand if needed. Frustum `SelectedHistory` and plain lists still work and take a single-copy path via `_prefix_kv`.

## Tests

Added `TestCosmosDreamsPrefixBuffer` (Modal CPU): buffer contents are bitwise equal to `append_kv_history` over mixed append sizes (full, sliding, sink+window, preallocated capacity), initial-block-over-window is rejected, and `_joint_attention` with `chunk_in_prefix` is bitwise equal to the concat path. `test_cosmos_dreams.py`: 61 passed, 1 skipped on Modal CPU. The 3 `test_offloaded_vae_uses_serial_decode` subtests fail identically on main in the CPU env (55 passed, same 3 failures on main).

## Benchmark

Real checkpoint (`nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual`), Modal L40S, base 9f6678aa3d vs this branch. 81 frames (21 latent), 480x640, seed 1, fixed synthetic input image, no actions, full-history default profile. 1 cold warmup run discarded, then 10 warm runs per variant, alternating. Full per-run data and tests are in the comment below.

| | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Rollout stage, mean (s) | 6.837 (sd 0.065) | 6.718 (sd 0.079) |
| Peak memory (MB) | 30960 | 29924 |
| Output mp4 md5 | identical across all 20 runs | identical across all 20 runs |

The rollout is 1.7% faster (95% CI 0.7% to 2.7%; Welch p = 0.0018, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0036). That is statistically significant but small at this size (short history, small chunk). Peak memory is about 1 GB lower. Caveats: noise input and null actions, one resolution and GPU, full-history profile only, runs share a container.

Earlier synthetic microbenchmark (L4, 12 layers, 16 heads / 4 KV heads, head dim 128, 512 text tokens, 256 tokens per frame, chunk of 4 frames, 4 denoise steps, framewise commits, QK norm and RoPE stubbed, plain SDPA): 1.04x to 1.08x, outputs bitwise equal, with gains growing with history length and shrinking as chunk size grows. Not a substitute for the real-checkpoint numbers above.

`cosmos3_sim_auto.py` and `nomas_kv_cache.py` are not touched.

issues.title: [sglang-miles] [Diffusion] Let a rollout request skip the VAE decode
issues.body:
## Motivation

Data-free DMD2 in miles-diffusion (radixark/miles_diffusion#343) trains only on the rollout trajectory: the student's input and x0 prediction from `dit_trajectory`, and the cond from `denoising_env`. With no reward model, nothing reads the decoded media of a training rollout. Every rollout request still runs the VAE decode (video and, for MiniMax H3, audio) and ships the decoded video. For H3 at 768p 16:9 5 s that is 124×768×1344×3 B = 384 MB per sample even as `uint8`, about 123 GB per 320-sample rollout through HTTP and msgpack.

## Modifications

- `RolloutRequest` / `SamplingParams`: `rollout_return_generated_output`, default `True` (no behavior change). It is a `SamplingParams` field without `batch_sig_exclude`, so requests that decode and requests that don't are never batched together.
- `rollout_output_without_decode` (`stages/decoding.py`): the `OutputBatch` with the rollout trajectory, trajectory timesteps / latents, metrics and usage, and no media.
- `DecodingStage.forward` and `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage.forward` return it first thing when the field is `False`, before loading or running a VAE. H3's `verify_output` accepts that output (no media, a rollout trajectory) and still rejects any other empty output.
- `rollout_generate` rejects a request with the field `False` whose output came back decoded anyway (400). Decoding stages that override `forward` without the check (LTX-2, Cosmos3, MOVA, ...) would otherwise decode silently; they can opt in the same way. `_build_response` takes the response count from `num_outputs_per_prompt` when there is no output.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-H3 (t2va, 2×B200 TP2, 768p 16:9 4 s = 1344×768 / 107 frames, 4 steps, `ode`, seed 1234, `rollout_video_dtype=uint8`, `rollout_return_dit_trajectory` and `rollout_return_denoising_env` on), on a tree with this commit and #46544 (audio in the response) on top of `sglang-miles` 2a2fb7310; the two touch separate response fields:

- With `rollout_return_generated_output=False`, `dit_trajectory` (latents `[5, 32256, 96]`, timesteps, sigmas, step indices), `denoising_env` (9 tensors) and `rollout_log_probs` are bitwise equal to the decoded request's; `generated_output` is `None`.
- With the default, the decoded request is unchanged: against `sglang-miles` 2a2fb7310 on the same request, the decoded video, `dit_trajectory`, `denoising_env` and `rollout_log_probs` are bitwise equal.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup, after one warm-up request:

| | decode on (6 runs) | `rollout_return_generated_output=False` (4 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` | 1.27 s | 0.0000 s |
| `inference_time_s` | 5.92-5.94 s | 4.66-4.67 s |
| response body | 396.2 MB | 63.7 MB |
| client wall time | 8.2-11.6 s | 5.6-7.0 s |

The remaining 63.7 MB is the full 5-latent trajectory; a DMD2 request that stops at a step and returns two latents ships about 25 MB.

## Tests

- `test_rollout_api.py`:
  - the field reaches the pipeline request (`Req`), and defaults to `True`;
  - `DecodingStage` and `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` return the request's trajectory without touching the VAE;
  - H3's output verification accepts the trajectory-only output and still rejects an empty output without a rollout trajectory;
  - a response without output has one entry per requested output, with the trajectory sliced per sample.
- 44 passed in `test_rollout_api.py`; 443 passed across the 29 unit files that touch decoding, H3, rollout and sampling params. `pre-commit run` on the changed files is clean.

issues.title: [Doc] diffusion/realtime: Document the session protocol shared by all realtime pipelines
issues.body:
## Motivation

The model cookbooks document each realtime model's `init` fields and event kinds. The parts every realtime pipeline shares are not written down anywhere, and a client author has to read `realtime_video_api.py` and `realtime_output_adapter.py` to find them:

- client messages must be binary MessagePack frames;
- a frame batch arrives either as one `frame_batch` message or as a `frame_batch_header` followed by a raw payload message;
- `chunk_stats` follows each chunk;
- an event applies to the chunk after the one being generated, and frame batches echo the `event_id` of the latest event their chunk sampled;
- what happens on an invalid `init`, an invalid event, `max_chunks`, a busy GPU slot, and a client disconnect.

## Modifications

Add a "Session Protocol" section to `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/realtime_models.mdx`, between "Supported Realtime Pipelines" and "Causal Cache Controls". It describes the current behavior on `main`, checked against the code:

- `FRAME_BATCH_PACK_OFFLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024` decides `frame_batch` vs `frame_batch_header` + payload, and `session.output_lock` keeps the header and its payload adjacent;
- `_send_output_and_log` sends `chunk_stats` after the chunk's frames;
- all four adapters (LingBot World, SANA-WM, HY-Nomas, Cosmos-Dreams) return `latest_sampled_event_id` from `get_realtime_event_id`;
- HY-Nomas (`end` event) and SANA-WM (a chunk with no frames) end a session by setting `max_chunks`, which closes with `1000` `generation complete`.

Three open fixes change single rows of the new tables: #48685 (text frames), #48686 (close code after a generation failure) and #48687 (error reasons). Whichever of these lands after this PR gets its row updated in the same PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Documentation only.

issues.title: [sglang-miles] Cut deterministic inference overhead on ROCm
issues.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference (`--enable-deterministic-inference`) is much slower than the default
on ROCm. Three kernels on the batch-invariant path are responsible
1.  residual RMSNorm has no batch-invariant kernel and falls back to eager PyTorch, the deterministic .
2.  GEMM uses one fixed tile config that wastes most of its tile on decode-shaped inputs.
3. and the unified prefill attention walks the whole KV length even for query blocks whose later keys are all masked.
This PR fixes all three. **ROCm only** — no CUDA path is touched.

## Modifications

Three commits, one per kernel:

1. **Fuse residual RMSNorm.** Add a Triton kernel for
   `x, residual = rms_norm(x + residual), x + residual`, so the pattern stops falling back to
   `forward_native`, which ran the add, square, mean, rsqrt and multiply as separate launches.
4. **Autotune the deterministic GEMM while staying batch invariant.** Split the choice in two:
   the K split is sized from K alone, and BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N / num_warps / num_stages come from
   the shape plus the card's CU count and LDS size. Only the K split can move the accumulation
   order, so only it has to ignore the batch.
5. **Bound the prefill attention loop by causality.** Stop the KV loop at the causal bound. A
   dropped tile would have added `exp(-inf) = 0` to the online softmax, so the output is
   bitwise identical, not an approximation.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_ops.py`: 6 passed, 54
  subtests passed.
- Bitwise batch invariance: a row computed alone equals the same row inside batches of 1 to
  2048, on every weight shape in Qwen3-0.6B, across all BLOCK_M transitions.
- End-to-end: logprobs for a prompt run alone are bitwise equal to the same prompt run inside
  a batch of 64.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), Qwen3-0.6B, single card. Decode tokens/s on a 4k prompt:

| batch | before | after | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 170.1 | 368.0 | 2.16x |
| 8 | 1130.2 | 1669.2 | 1.48x |
| 32 | 1954.3 | 2705.8 | 1.38x |
| 64 | 2410.1 | 3257.7 | 1.35x |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

No new tests: the existing batch-invariant unit test above already covers these ops, and no
user-facing behavior changed, so there is nothing to document.

issues.title: [DSV4] Use mhc_pre's split-K pre-norm GEMM in the mhc_fused_post_pre fallback
issues.body:
## Motivation

`mhc_fused_post_pre` is the mHC layer boundary DeepSeek-V4 runs between every pair of layers. Above `fma_token_threshold = 32` tokens it splits into `mhc_post` + a pre-norm GEMM, and when `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` is off it takes a fallback whose comment reads:

```python
else:
    # Fallback mirrors mhc_pre when DeepGEMM prenorm is disabled.
```

It does not mirror `mhc_pre`. In the same file and the same configuration, `mhc_pre` runs `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_splitk_kernel` for any batch up to 2048 tokens, while this fallback calls `_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_dispatch()` — the non-split kernel, whose grid is `T.Kernel(T.ceildiv(num_tokens, token_block))` with `token_block=32`. At a decode batch of 40 that is **2 thread blocks**, so 2 SMs stream the whole 1.5 MiB fp32 `fn` matrix while the rest of the device idles.

Measured standalone at DeepSeek-V4-Flash shapes (`hidden_size=4096`, `hc_mult=4`, so `hc_hidden_size=16384`), 40 tokens:

| | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120) | RTX 4090 (sm_89) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `mhc_fused_post_pre`, plain fallback | 84.1 us | 103.5 us |
| `mhc_fused_post_pre`, `mhc_pre`'s split-K | **12.4 us** | **12.5 us** |

The op itself only has ~12 us of work in it: at 40 tokens the input is 40 x 4 x 4096 bf16 (1.3 MB) and the weights are 1.5 MiB, so the whole boundary is a few microseconds of traffic plus launch overhead. The remaining 72 us is one kernel occupying two SMs. Over the 43 layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash that is **3.1 ms per decode step** on sm_120 that no configuration needs to pay.

**Who reaches this.** A DeepSeek-V4 decode batch above 32 with the DeepGEMM pre-norm path off, i.e. any of:

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0` set directly;
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0`, which is exactly the configuration in #29738 (`NameError: name 'deep_gemm' is not defined` in `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, being fixed in #38442) — turning the pre-norm flag off is the workaround people land on;
- a DeepGEMM build without support for the running arch.

Batch <= 32 takes the FMA path and never sees it, which is why a batch-size-dependent 6x on a layer-boundary op has gone unreported.

The two have differed since `mhc_fused_post_pre` was introduced in #25976 — `mhc_pre` had already moved to the split-K kernel in #23882 three weeks earlier. It cost nothing at the time, because the fused path was opt-in; #34019 and #35214 made it the default in August, and today's `main` (`ccfa120dae`) still takes the plain kernel here.

## Root cause

`mhc_pre` and `mhc_fused_post_pre` each open-code the same "no DeepGEMM" decision, and only `mhc_pre` was updated when the split-K kernel landed.

`mhc_pre`:

```python
if num_tokens <= 2048:
    ...
    kernel_0, _ = mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_splitk_kernel(..., split_k=n_splits_pre, ...)
    gemm_last_dim = 32                 # partials, stage_1 folded into big_fuse
    big_fuse_n_splits = n_splits_pre   # 32
```

`mhc_fused_post_pre`:

```python
n_splits = 1
_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_dispatch()(...)   # grid = ceil(num_tokens / 32)
```

The two kernels compute the same thing; they differ only in how the `hc_hidden_size = 16384` reduction is parallelized. The split-K kernel launches `(ceil(num_tokens / 32), split_k)` blocks with `split_k = 32`, so each block reads 1/32 of `fn` and the reduction over splits is folded into `mhc_pre_big_fuse`, which already takes an `n_splits` argument. The plain kernel gives one block per 32 tokens and no split at all, so its occupancy is set entirely by the batch size.

CUDA profile of the boundary at 40 tokens on sm_120 (us per call):

```text
before:  76.6  mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_tilelang_kernel
          4.0  mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang_kernel
          3.1  mhc_post_tilelang_kernel

after:    4.3  mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang_kernel
          4.1  mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_splitk_stage_0_kernel
          3.0  mhc_post_tilelang_kernel
```

Nothing else moves: the split-K partials cost `big_fuse` 0.3 us more, and the 76.6 us kernel becomes a 4.1 us one.

## Modifications

Extract the split-K launch into `_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_splitk`, shared by both call sites, so the branch cannot drift again — the duplication is what caused this. The kernel selection constants come with it:

```python
MHC_PRE_SPLITK_MAX_TOKENS = 2048
MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK = {16384: 256, 28672: 128}
```

`mhc_pre` keeps its exact behaviour; its inline `if hc_hidden_size == 16384 / elif 28672 / else raise` moves into the helper unchanged. `mhc_fused_post_pre` takes the helper on the same condition, tracks the resulting last GEMM dim in `gemm_last_dim` (32 for split-K partials, `hc_mult3` otherwise) the way `mhc_pre` already does, and gains the same `n_splits_pre: int = 32` parameter.

One deliberate asymmetry: for an `hc_hidden_size` the split-K kernel is not specialized for, `mhc_pre` raises `NotImplementedError` but `mhc_fused_post_pre` has always accepted any size through the plain kernel. The new branch is therefore an `elif` guarded on `hc_hidden_size in MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK`, and unqualified shapes keep the plain kernel rather than starting to raise. Batches above `MHC_PRE_SPLITK_MAX_TOKENS` also keep it, matching `mhc_pre` and the measurements below.

No new JIT compilation: `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_splitk_kernel` is `functools.cache`d on `(hc_mult3, hc_hidden_size, split_k, token_block, hidden_block)` and the fallback passes the arguments `mhc_pre` already passes, so `prewarm_mhc_pre` covers it.

`test_mhc_fused_post_pre_no_deepgemm_matches_mhc_pre` asserts the branch, not just the numbers. With `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` overridden off it counts `_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_dispatch` calls across an `mhc_post` + `mhc_pre` reference and an `mhc_fused_post_pre` call at 40 and 64 tokens, and requires zero from both. **This is the assertion that fails on the pre-fix code** — a numeric-only test would not, because the plain kernel is correct, just slow:

```text
E  AssertionError: mhc_fused_post_pre took the plain pre-norm GEMM where mhc_pre uses split-K
E  assert 1 == 0
```

It then checks the outputs against the unfused sequence at the tolerances the neighbouring test uses. The TP-group bypass the existing test needed is factored into `_bypass_tp_group` and shared.

## Accuracy Tests

Switching a reduction from one accumulator to 32 partials changes fp32 summation order, so the honest question is not whether the two kernels agree bit-for-bit but which is closer to the truth. Against a float64 reference of the same `mhc_post` -> `mhc_pre` sequence (both kernels consume a bit-identical bf16 `residual_cur`, so this isolates the GEMM), mean `|diff|` / mean `|ref|` on sm_120:

| tokens | `post` plain | `post` split-K | `comb` plain | `comb` split-K | `layer_input` plain | `layer_input` split-K |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 40 | 5.855e-05 | **5.530e-05** | 8.404e-05 | **7.905e-05** | 1.413e-03 | 1.413e-03 |
| 64 | 5.648e-05 | **5.331e-05** | 8.261e-05 | **7.761e-05** | 1.413e-03 | 1.413e-03 |
| 512 | 5.473e-05 | **5.158e-05** | 7.878e-05 | **7.422e-05** | 1.410e-03 | 1.410e-03 |
| 2048 | 5.342e-05 | **5.021e-05** | 8.050e-05 | **7.575e-05** | 1.410e-03 | 1.410e-03 |

The split-K path is consistently **more** accurate on `post` and `comb` — pairwise summation over 32 partials loses less than one long accumulator — and identical on `layer_input`, whose error is bf16 output rounding, not the GEMM. `residual` is bit-identical (it comes from `mhc_post`, untouched). Direct plain-vs-split-K deltas are correspondingly small: `post` <= 1.7e-05 and `comb` <= 7.8e-06 absolute at 40 tokens, and 327 of 163840 `layer_input` elements differ by more than one bf16 ulp.

Unit tests, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mhc_kernels.py`:

```text
repo defaults (DeepGEMM pre-norm on):        28 passed
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0:            28 passed
```

28 = the 24 existing cases plus the 4 new ones. Both configurations were run because the changed branch is only reachable in the second.

No model eval was run. The DeepGEMM path — the default, and what CI exercises — is untouched, and on the fallback the change is a reduction-order difference that measures closer to a float64 reference than what it replaces.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`mhc_fused_post_pre` alone, CUDA-graph replay, 200 replays, `hidden_size=4096` / `hc_mult=4` / `norm_weight` set, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0`. "before" is the plain fallback, "after" is split-K; A/B in one process so the two share compilation and allocator state.

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120):

| tokens | before | after | speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 24 (FMA path, unchanged) | 16.5 us | 16.5 us | 1.00x |
| 33 | 84.1 us | 12.4 us | 6.80x |
| 40 | 84.1 us | 12.4 us | 6.80x |
| 64 | 84.1 us | 12.4 us | 6.80x |
| 128 | 85.2 us | 12.4 us | 6.89x |
| 512 | 94.3 us | 30.8 us | 3.06x |
| 2048 | 186.0 us | 158.7 us | 1.17x |

RTX 4090 (sm_89):

| tokens | before | after | speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 24 (FMA path, unchanged) | 14.4 us | 14.4 us | 1.00x |
| 33 | 103.5 us | 12.5 us | 8.30x |
| 40 | 103.5 us | 12.5 us | 8.28x |
| 64 | 104.0 us | 12.8 us | 8.11x |
| 128 | 104.7 us | 14.5 us | 7.24x |
| 512 | 109.3 us | 42.0 us | 2.60x |
| 2048 | 272.2 us | 269.1 us | 1.01x |

The shape of the curve is the diagnosis. Below 32 tokens nothing changes, because that is the FMA path. From 33 to 128 the plain kernel is flat at ~84 us regardless of batch — it is not doing more work, it is doing the same work on 2 to 4 SMs — while split-K is flat at 12.4 us. By 512 tokens the plain grid is wide enough to matter and the gap narrows; by 2048, `MHC_PRE_SPLITK_MAX_TOKENS`, they converge, which is why both `mhc_pre` and this fallback stop using split-K there.

For DeepSeek-V4-Flash (43 layers) at a decode batch of 40 on sm_120, 43 x 71.7 us = **3.1 ms per decode step** returned to the model. Standalone the kernel has the device to itself; in a real forward pass it is competing for SMs with the rest of the layer, so this is a floor rather than an estimate. No full-model end-to-end benchmark is claimed here — the numbers above are `main` plus this patch and are exactly what the attached script reproduces.

<summary>bench_mhc_fused_post_pre.py</summary>

```python
"""Repro for the mhc_fused_post_pre pre-norm GEMM fallback.

Times the layer-boundary op at DeepSeek-V4-Flash decode shapes with the
DeepGEMM pre-norm path disabled, which is the configuration that reaches the
fallback branch.  On a patched tree it also A/Bs against the old plain-GEMM
fallback by emptying MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK, and reports the output delta.

    SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0 python bench_mhc_fused_post_pre.py
"""

import contextlib
import os
import sys

import torch

os.environ.setdefault("SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM", "0")

import sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.mhc as mhc  # noqa: E402

# Single-process kernel bench: no TP group, no symmetric-memory pool.
mhc.use_symmetric_memory = lambda *a, **k: contextlib.nullcontext()
mhc.get_tp_group = lambda: None
mhc.is_allocation_symmetric = lambda: False
mhc.is_dsa_prefill_cp_round_robin_split = lambda: False

# DeepSeek-V4-Flash: hidden 4096, hc_mult 4 -> hc_hidden_size 16384.
HIDDEN, HC_MULT, SINKHORN, EPS = 4096, 4, 20, 1e-6
HC_MULT3 = HC_MULT * 2 + HC_MULT * HC_MULT
HAS_SPLITK = hasattr(mhc, "MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK")


def make_inputs(num_tokens):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    d = "cuda"
    return dict(
        x=torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN, device=d, dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1,
        residual=torch.randn(
            num_tokens, HC_MULT, HIDDEN, device=d, dtype=torch.bfloat16
        )
        * 0.1,
        post_layer_mix=torch.rand(num_tokens, HC_MULT, 1, device=d),
        comb_res_mix=torch.rand(num_tokens, HC_MULT, HC_MULT, device=d) / HC_MULT,
        fn=torch.randn(HC_MULT3, HC_MULT * HIDDEN, device=d) * 0.01,
        hc_scale=torch.tensor([0.5, 0.25, 0.25], device=d),
        hc_base=torch.randn(HC_MULT3, device=d) * 0.1,
        norm_weight=torch.ones(HIDDEN, device=d, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
    )


def call(t):
    return mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre(
        t["x"],
        t["residual"],
        t["post_layer_mix"],
        t["comb_res_mix"],
        t["fn"],
        t["hc_scale"],
        t["hc_base"],
        EPS,
        EPS,
        EPS,
        2.0,
        SINKHORN,
        norm_weight=t["norm_weight"],
        norm_eps=EPS,
    )


def time_us(t, reps=200):
    for _ in range(5):
        call(t)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    g, s = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(), torch.cuda.Stream()
    s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(s):
        for _ in range(2):
            call(t)
        with torch.cuda.graph(g, stream=s):
            call(t)
    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    a, b = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
    a.record()
    for _ in range(reps):
        g.replay()
    b.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return a.elapsed_time(b) / reps * 1e3


@contextlib.contextmanager
def force_plain_gemm():
    """Route the fallback to the pre-fix plain kernel."""
    saved = mhc.MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK
    mhc.MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK = {}
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        mhc.MHC_PRE_SPLITK_HIDDEN_BLOCK = saved


def fp64_reference(t):
    """mhc_post -> mhc_pre in float64, without the fused RMSNorm.

    Both kernels consume the same bf16 residual_cur, so this isolates what the
    pre-norm GEMM and its reduction contribute to the error.
    """
    x, res = t["x"].double(), t["residual"].double()
    residual_cur = (
        t["post_layer_mix"].double() * x.unsqueeze(1)
        + (t["comb_res_mix"].double().unsqueeze(-1) * res.unsqueeze(2)).sum(dim=1)
    ).bfloat16()  # the kernels round here too; residual_cur is bit-identical

    n = HC_MULT
    flat = residual_cur.view(residual_cur.shape[0], -1).double()
    rsqrt = torch.rsqrt(flat.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + EPS)
    mixes = (flat @ t["fn"].double().T) * rsqrt
    scale, base = t["hc_scale"].double(), t["hc_base"].double()
    pre = torch.sigmoid(mixes[:, :n] * scale[0] + base[:n]) + EPS
    post = 2.0 * torch.sigmoid(mixes[:, n : 2 * n] * scale[1] + base[n : 2 * n])
    comb = mixes[:, 2 * n :].view(-1, n, n) * scale[2] + base[2 * n :].view(n, n)
    comb = comb.softmax(-1) + EPS
    comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2, keepdim=True) + EPS)
    for _ in range(SINKHORN - 1):
        comb = comb / (comb.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + EPS)
        comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2, keepdim=True) + EPS)
    layer_input = (pre.unsqueeze(-1) * residual_cur.double()).sum(dim=1)
    return post.unsqueeze(-1), comb, layer_input


def accuracy(counts):
    """Error of each fallback against a float64 reference (no RMSNorm)."""
    print("Error vs float64 reference (mean |diff| / mean |ref|):")
    for n in counts:
        t = make_inputs(n)
        with torch.inference_mode():
            new = mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre(
                t["x"], t["residual"], t["post_layer_mix"], t["comb_res_mix"],
                t["fn"], t["hc_scale"], t["hc_base"], EPS, EPS, EPS, 2.0, SINKHORN,
            )
            with force_plain_gemm():
                ref = mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre(
                    t["x"], t["residual"], t["post_layer_mix"], t["comb_res_mix"],
                    t["fn"], t["hc_scale"], t["hc_base"], EPS, EPS, EPS, 2.0, SINKHORN,
                )
        gold = fp64_reference(t)
        out = [f"tokens={n:5d}"]
        for name, g, a, b in zip(("post", "comb", "layer_input"), gold, ref[1:], new[1:]):
            rel = lambda v: ((v.double() - g).abs().mean() / g.abs().mean()).item()
            out.append(f"{name}: plain {rel(a):.3e}  split-K {rel(b):.3e}")
        print("  " + "   ".join(out))


def kernels(t, tag):
    from torch.profiler import ProfilerActivity, profile

    for _ in range(3):
        call(t)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
        for _ in range(20):
            call(t)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
    rows = sorted(
        (
            (e.key[:60], e.device_time_total / 20)
            for e in prof.key_averages()
            if e.device_time_total > 0 and "Memcpy" not in e.key
        ),
        key=lambda r: -r[1],
    )
    print(f"  [{tag}] top CUDA kernels, us/call:")
    for name, us in rows[:4]:
        print(f"      {us:8.1f}  {name}")


def main():
    counts = [int(a) for a in sys.argv[1:]] or [24, 33, 40, 64, 128, 512, 2048]
    print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), "| split-K fallback:", HAS_SPLITK)
    if HAS_SPLITK and os.environ.get("BENCH_ACCURACY"):
        accuracy(counts)
    names = ("residual", "post", "comb", "layer_input")
    for n in counts:
        t = make_inputs(n)
        after = time_us(t)
        if not HAS_SPLITK:
            print(f"tokens={n:5d}  main {after:8.1f} us")
            continue
        new = [o.clone() for o in call(t)]
        with force_plain_gemm():
            before = time_us(t)
            ref = [o.clone() for o in call(t)]
        deltas = []
        for name, a, b in zip(names, ref, new):
            af, bf = a.float(), b.float()
            d = (af - bf).abs()
            if a.dtype == torch.bfloat16:
                # bf16 keeps 8 significand bits, so one ulp is a 2**-8
                # relative step; count elements that differ by more than that.
                over = (d > 2.0**-8 * af.abs()).sum().item()
                deltas.append(f"{name} {over}/{a.numel()} over 1 bf16 ulp")
            else:
                deltas.append(f"{name} max {d.max().item():.1e} abs")
        print(
            f"tokens={n:5d}  before {before:8.1f} us   after {after:8.1f} us"
            f"   {before / after:5.2f}x   " + ", ".join(deltas)
        )
        if os.environ.get("BENCH_KERNELS"):
            with force_plain_gemm():
                kernels(t, "before")
            kernels(t, "after")


main()
```

issues.title: [Fix] Normalize MiniCPM Lightning output across TP ranks
issues.body:
## Motivation

MiniCPM's Lightning attention layers apply RMS normalization across the combined output of all attention heads. With tensor parallelism, each rank holds a subset of those heads but currently computes the normalization denominator from its own subset. Different activation magnitudes between ranks therefore produce a different result from full-width normalization.

## Modifications

Reduce the FP32 mean-square statistics across tensor-parallel ranks before applying each rank's normalization weights. The TP=1 path keeps its existing implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regression covers unequal and zero-energy shards at TP=1, 2, and 4. A separate check using the real SGLang collective on two RTX 5090 GPUs matched full-width PyTorch RMS normalization for FP32 and BF16 inputs.

Real TP2 MiniCPM-SALA NVFP4 activations were also checked against a full-width FP32 reference rounded to BF16. Maximum absolute errors before output gating and projection were:

| Phase | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prefill | 2.3125 | 0.00390625 |
| Decode | 1.1875 | 0 |

Both corrected results satisfy `atol=rtol=1/128`. Separate TP2 serving smoke tests completed without request errors with decode CUDA graphs enabled.

PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_minicpm_output_norm.py

issues.title: [LoRA][MoE] NVFP4 LoRA on FlashInfer-CUTLASS MoE backend
issues.body:
## Motivation

`flashinfer_cutlass` is one of the supported NVFP4 MoE backends on SM100 and the required choice for some configurations (e.g. FP4 all-gather dispatch). It calls `flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe` as a single black-box kernel that runs the full MoE forward in one shot, leaving no point between W13 and W2 where a LoRA delta can be injected. Combining `--enable-lora` with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass` therefore crashes today. This PR makes the two compose so an NVFP4 MoE checkpoint can be served with a LoRA adapter on `flashinfer_cutlass`, with the same `--enable-lora` ergonomics that the existing Marlin / Triton LoRA paths already provide.

## Approach

The fused NVFP4 MoE kernel is broken open into its constituent FP4 group GEMMs, and the standard `after_gate_up` / `after_down` LoRA hooks (already used by `MarlinLoraRunnerCore`) are inserted between them. A new `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore` runs the unfused pipeline only when `--enable-lora` is set; non-LoRA `flashinfer_cutlass` continues to take the fused fast path through `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.apply` unchanged. The runner per layer executes: expert-id normalization → FP4 input quant → cutlass FP4 group GEMM (W13, expert-sorted) → `hooks.after_gate_up` over `[M, topk, 2N]` → Triton SwiGLU activation (with `[Up\|Gate]` swap when needed) → FP4 intermediate quant → cutlass FP4 group GEMM (W2) → `hooks.after_down` → Triton combine (un-sort + fp32 router-weight + sum). The LoRA hooks read and write the expert-sorted tensors directly via a `c_map` indirection, so no extra shuffle_rows bridge is needed.

## Key design decisions

- **Reuse the existing LoRA hook contract.** Adding `after_gate_up` / `after_down` callbacks to the runner means the LoRA kernels do not need a backend-specific delta API; the same `fused_moe_lora` Triton path used by Marlin and Triton MoE backends works on FlashInfer-CUTLASS unchanged. This keeps the LoRA surface uniform across MoE backends, lowers test surface, and matches the project's "any LoRA on any MoE backend" direction.

- **Single LoRA hook construction path.** `build_lora_hooks` no longer special-cases eager no-LoRA batches. CUDA graph capture records the LoRA hooks unconditionally after upstream removed the dual LoRA/no-LoRA graph variant, so eager mode now follows the same hook-construction path. For MoE hooks, `adapter_enabled` masks only requested slots with `rank > 0`, and virtual-expert token mapping converts inactive slots to `-1`; both eager and CUDA graph then rely on the same kernel-side no-op behavior while preserving the adapter-enabled gating used by the captured graph.

- **`c_map` indirection on `fused_moe_lora`.** The fused_moe_lora kernel was extended with `USE_C_MAP_INPUT` / `USE_C_MAP_OUTPUT` constexpr branches so the LoRA hooks can read and write the expert-sorted layout directly. Without this, the runner would have to wrap each hook with a triple `shuffle_rows` (sorted→token-major before the hook, hook in token-major, token-major→sorted after): three extra global memory passes per hook, two hooks per layer, 60 layers. The constexpr branches mean non-LoRA paths and non-MoE LoRA paths get identical SASS to before; only the new sorted-layout path takes the new code.

- **LoRA-local Triton epilogue for activation and combine.** Kimi-K2.5's W13 stores `[Up | Gate]` (Up first, Gate second) instead of the usual `[Gate | Up]`, and the final combine should keep router weights in fp32 to match fused-Cutlass behavior more closely. The final PR handles both with Triton kernels under `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/cutlass_fp4_moe.py`: one for swapped SwiGLU activation, and one for un-sort + fp32 router-weight + top-k reduction. Earlier revisions tried to extend the shared JIT activation kernel and `sgl-kernel` combine kernel; those common-kernel changes are intentionally not part of the final PR.

- **Virtual experts `c_map` bridge plus gated-MLP fix.** `merged_experts_fused_moe_lora_add` (the virtual-experts kernel) gained matching `c_map` support so it can also write into the expert-sorted layout, and its expand stage now iterates the gate and up columns instead of only the rank-r prefix. The Cutlass FP4 LoRA path therefore works for both classic and virtual-experts adapters, and the gated-MLP fix is correctness rather than just optimization: without it the virtual-experts path dropped the up-proj half for Kimi-style gated activations.

## File map

- `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runner_cutlass_fp4.py` (new) — `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore` + `CutlassFp4MoeQuantInfo`.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py` — wires `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore` under `flashinfer_cutlass + lora_enabled`.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py` — `get_cutlass_fp4_quant_info` builder, pre-expanded `[E]` input scales, `w13_swap_halves` tracking.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/layers.py` — `FusedMoEWithLoRA.__init__` calls the new builder for the cutlass branch and forwards upstream MoE runner attributes required by the rebased DeepSeek/Kimi MoE path.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runners.py` — standard MoE LoRA hook construction plus sorted-layout / `c_map` propagation to hooks.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` — `USE_C_MAP_INPUT/OUTPUT` constexpr branches.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/cutlass_fp4_moe.py` — LoRA-local Triton activation and combine kernels for the Cutlass FP4 runner.
- `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/virtual_experts.py` — matching `c_map` support, gated-MLP expand fix.
- `test/registered/lora/test_virtual_experts_kernels.py` — CUDA regression coverage for token-to-LoRA mapping with padded request tables.
- `test/registered/lora/test_lora_kimi_k25_logprob_diff.py` — nightly Kimi NVFP4 + LoRA coverage for the `modelopt_fp4 + flashinfer_cutlass + virtual experts` path.

## Accuracy

Verified on 2 GB200 nodes with `Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4` + rank-16 LoRA adapter. The main accuracy check uses the 1809-token sequence from [`compare_sample_train_data.pt`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yushengsu/lora-diff-Kimi-K2.5/blob/main/compare_sample_train_data.pt), sends `max_new_tokens=0`, returns input-token logprobs, drops the first token position, and compares the remaining 1808 positions across serving variants. All rows below used two-node TP=8 with EP disabled (`ep_size=1`).

- **A** — `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, no LoRA.
- **B** — `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --enable-lora --lora-paths alpha=...`, request sent **without** `lora_path` (this PR's path through `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore` with adapter masks disabled).
- **B-lora** — same as B, request sent with `lora_path=alpha`.
- **C** — same as B, server launched with `--lora-use-virtual-experts`, request sent **without** `lora_path`.
- **C-lora** — same as B-lora, server launched with `--lora-use-virtual-experts`.

| Pair | mean abs | max abs | half squared mean | identical |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A vs B | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | true |
| A vs C | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | true |
| B-lora vs C-lora | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | true |

The final stack preserves fused-Cutlass no-LoRA behavior exactly on the LoRA-enabled server, and virtual experts match the non-virtual active-LoRA path exactly on this dataset capture.

## Performance

Run on two-node TP=8 GB200, Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4, `bench_one_batch_server`, `bs=32`, `input_len=1024`, `output_len=2048`, CUDA graph enabled, EP disabled (`ep_size=1`), `--load-format auto`, and `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`. The table reports the mean of three measured runs per row; the client warmup run is excluded. All rows used the same current PR branch, default attention selection (`attention_backend=trtllm_mla`, `prefill_attention_backend=None`, `decode_attention_backend=None`).

| Variant | Server path | Request LoRA | Total latency (s) | Prefill total / TTFT (s) | Prefill tok/s | Decode total time (s) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | `flashinfer_cutlass` fused | no | 47.1350 | 0.8538 | 38378.66 | 46.2812 | 1416.04 |
| B | unfused Cutlass LoRA runner | no | 94.3261 | 1.4689 | 22308.13 | 92.8572 | 705.77 |
| B-lora | unfused Cutlass LoRA runner | `alpha` | 111.9190 | 1.8646 | 17573.83 | 110.0543 | 595.54 |
| C | unfused runner + `--lora-use-virtual-experts` | no | 67.5686 | 1.2736 | 25728.88 | 66.2950 | 988.55 |
| C-lora | unfused runner + `--lora-use-virtual-experts` | `alpha` | 63.7587 | 1.4356 | 22824.99 | 62.3231 | 1051.55 |

As a non-NVFP4 sanity check, I also reran Qwen FP8 MoE LoRA serving on 1 GB200 node with `bench_one_batch_server`, `bs=16`, `input_len=1024`, `output_len=2048`. These rows compare the main/base commit used for the rebase against the final overall PR branch and report mean decode throughput.

| Model | TP/EP | Request | Main/base output tok/s | Overall output tok/s | Delta |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-FP8 | 4/4 | no-LoRA | 1897.89 | 1878.60 | -1.02% |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-FP8 | 4/4 | LoRA `alpha` | 1807.76 | 1794.42 | -0.74% |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 | 4/1 | no-LoRA | 1645.15 | 1644.76 | -0.02% |

Qwen no-LoRA accuracy was exact against main/base. Qwen LoRA on the final PR matched the canonical no-virtual-experts/eager path; the old base CUDA-graph virtual-experts capture was the divergent reference, so that caveat is tracked separately from this NVFP4 support change.

issues.title: [2/4][LoRA] Avoid NVFP4 Cutlass LoRA layout bridges
issues.body:
Reference: split from the overall PR [sgl-project/sglang#25202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25202).

## Motivation

PR1 proves the LoRA hook integration but still has unnecessary layout traffic around the hooks. The Cutlass FP4 GEMMs naturally operate in expert-sorted pair layout, while the original hook contract expects token-major layout. Bridging those layouts with explicit shuffles costs extra memory bandwidth per MoE layer.

## Approach

This PR extends the MoE LoRA hook kernels with an optional `c_map` indirection so they can read and write expert-sorted buffers directly. It also adds a `swap_halves` mode to the JIT activation kernel for Kimi-K2.5's `[Up|Gate]` W13 layout.

## Key Changes

- Add `c_map` and `sorted_layout` propagation through `LoRAInfo`.
- Extend `fused_moe_lora` with `USE_C_MAP_INPUT` and `USE_C_MAP_OUTPUT` constexpr paths.
- Use the sorted-layout hook path in `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore`.
- Add `swap_halves` to the JIT `silu_and_mul` activation path.
- Bump the activation JIT module key to `activation_swap_halves` because the exported JIT function ABI now has the extra `swap_halves` argument; this avoids loading stale cached modules built with the old 3-argument ABI.
- Keep virtual experts guarded out of this PR; PR4 adds that support.

## Accuracy

Same two-node TP=8 setup as PR1. Accuracy captures use the 1809-token sequence from [`compare_sample_train_data.pt`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yushengsu/lora-diff-Kimi-K2.5/blob/main/compare_sample_train_data.pt), request `max_new_tokens=0`, return input-token logprobs, and compare 1808 positions.

| Pair | mean abs | max abs | half squared mean | identical |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| B vs PR2 C-nolora | 0.102540 | 3.790158 | 0.053243 | false |
| PR1 C-lora vs PR2 C-lora | 0.235814 | 2.668981 | 0.087248 | false |

This PR is primarily the sorted-layout/perf slice. The no-LoRA passthrough remains at the PR1 accuracy level; PR3 fixes the fused-Cutlass parity gap by keeping router factors in fp32 during the final combine.

## Performance

`bs=32`, `input_len=1024`, `output_len=2048`.

| Variant | prefill time (s) | prefill tok/s | decode time (s) | decode tok/s | total latency (s) | overall tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PR1 C-nolora | 1.41 | 23221 | 425.36 | 154.07 | 426.77 | 230.35 |
| PR1 C-lora | 2.11 | 15516 | 415.83 | 157.60 | 417.94 | 235.21 |
| PR2 C-nolora | 1.39 | 23620 | 422.22 | 155.22 | 423.60 | 232.07 |
| PR2 C-lora | 2.02 | 16196 | 412.41 | 158.91 | 414.43 | 237.20 |

The sorted-layout path improves active-LoRA latency by 3.51s at this shape and also removes the stale JIT ABI failure observed when switching from PR1 to PR2 on a pod with an existing activation cache.

## Validation

- `python -m py_compile` on the touched Python files.
- `git diff --check`.
- Two-node C server launch after a PR1 run with an existing JIT cache, confirming the activation module key fix.
- Dataset-based accuracy capture, no-LoRA perf, and active-LoRA perf on `mnnvl-yanbin-0/1`.

issues.body:
Reference: split from the overall PR [sgl-project/sglang#25202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25202).

## Motivation

The non-virtual expert LoRA path works after PR1-PR3, but the virtual-expert path needs matching sorted-layout support. Without it, enabling virtual experts either needs layout bridges or can write/read the LoRA delta in the wrong row layout. There is also a gated-MLP correctness issue where the virtual-expert expand stage can drop the up half.

## Approach

This PR extends the virtual-expert LoRA kernels and the fused MoE expand-add helper with `c_map` output remapping, then wires that through the standard MoE LoRA hooks. It also fixes the gated expand stage by expanding both gate and up slices.

Virtual experts are enabled with the server flag `--lora-use-virtual-experts`.

## Key Changes

- Add sorted-layout `c_map` support to `merged_experts_fused_moe_lora_add`.
- Extend `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` with a `c_map` output remap for `fuse_add_to_output=True`.
- Fix gated virtual-expert expand by running the expand over both gate and up slices instead of only the first rank slice.
- Remove the temporary virtual-experts guard from `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore`.
- Keep non-VE C behavior aligned with PR3.

issues.title: [1/4][LoRA] Add NVFP4 Cutlass MoE LoRA runner
issues.body:
Reference: split from the overall PR [sgl-project/sglang#25202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25202).

## Motivation

`flashinfer_cutlass` calls the NVFP4 MoE as one fused kernel, so there is no point between W13 and W2 where the existing LoRA hooks can add the adapter delta. Enabling LoRA with this backend therefore needs a runner that exposes the same `after_gate_up` and `after_down` hook points used by the existing MoE LoRA runners.

## Approach

This PR adds `CutlassFp4LoraRunnerCore`, an unfused NVFP4 Cutlass MoE pipeline used only when `--enable-lora` is active with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`. Non-LoRA `flashinfer_cutlass` serving continues to use the existing fused backend.

The runner performs EP-local expert remap, FP4 input quantization, Cutlass FP4 group GEMM for W13, standard LoRA gate/up hook, activation, FP4 intermediate quantization, Cutlass FP4 group GEMM for W2, standard LoRA down hook, and final combine.

## Key Changes

- Add `python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_moe_runner_cutlass_fp4.py`.
- Wire the runner from the MoE runner factory for `flashinfer_cutlass + lora_enabled`.
- Build and pass NVFP4 Cutlass quantization metadata through `modelopt_quant.py`.
- Add `LoRAInfo.has_active_lora` and skip eager zero-LoRA hook launches.
- Disable the FP4 all-gather dispatch path for LoRA configurations because this runner expects bf16 hidden states and re-quantizes locally.

## Accuracy

Tested on `mnnvl-yanbin-0/1` with two-node TP=8, `Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4`, and the rank-16 `alpha` adapter. Accuracy captures use the 1809-token sequence from [`compare_sample_train_data.pt`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yushengsu/lora-diff-Kimi-K2.5/blob/main/compare_sample_train_data.pt), request `max_new_tokens=0`, return input-token logprobs, and compare the 1808 positions after dropping the first token.

Baselines:

- A: `flashinfer_trtllm`, no LoRA.
- B: `flashinfer_cutlass`, fused, no LoRA.
- C: `flashinfer_cutlass --enable-lora`, request without `lora_path`.

| Pair | mean abs | max abs | half squared mean | identical |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A vs B | 0.101421 | 3.921772 | 0.065445 | false |
| B vs PR1 C-nolora | 0.102540 | 3.790158 | 0.053243 | false |

PR1 proves the path runs, and a separate active-LoRA capture with `lora_path=alpha` completed on the same dataset. The no-LoRA passthrough is not yet identical to fused Cutlass; PR3 addresses that combine-precision gap.

## Performance

Two-node TP=8, `bs=32`, `input_len=1024`, `output_len=2048`, FA4 prefill, FlashInfer decode. Values are the measured JSONL pass from `bench_one_batch_server`.

| Variant | prefill time (s) | prefill tok/s | decode time (s) | decode tok/s | total latency (s) | overall tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A trtllm | 0.95 | 34329 | 428.72 | 152.87 | 429.67 | 228.79 |
| B cutlass fused | 0.85 | 38332 | 441.72 | 148.37 | 442.57 | 222.12 |
| PR1 C-nolora | 1.41 | 23221 | 425.36 | 154.07 | 426.77 | 230.35 |
| PR1 C-lora | 2.11 | 15516 | 415.83 | 157.60 | 417.94 | 235.21 |

- `python -m py_compile` on the touched Python files.
- `git diff --check`.
- Two-node server launch, dataset-based accuracy capture, no-LoRA perf, and active-LoRA perf on `mnnvl-yanbin-0/1`.

issues.title: [3/4][LoRA] Improve NVFP4 Cutlass MoE combine accuracy
issues.body:
Reference: split from the overall PR [sgl-project/sglang#25202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25202).

## Motivation

The PR2 unfused Cutlass path still has a visible input-logprob gap against the fused FlashInfer-Cutlass backend. The main difference is the final combine: the fused backend applies router weights in fp32, while the existing combine kernel path downcast router weights to the output dtype before multiply/sum.

## Approach

This PR extends `apply_shuffle_mul_sum` to accept fp32 router factors and uses fp32 `topk_weights.reshape(-1)` in the NVFP4 Cutlass LoRA runner's final combine. Existing same-dtype factor callers keep the old behavior.

## Key Changes

- Add a fp32-factor specialization to `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/prepare_moe_input.cu`.
- Use fp32 router factors in `cutlass_moe.py` and the NVFP4 Cutlass LoRA runner where the fused backend keeps that precision.
- Keep the kernel ABI backward compatible for existing bf16/fp16 factor callers.

## Accuracy

Same two-node TP=8 setup as PR1. Accuracy captures use the 1809-token sequence from [`compare_sample_train_data.pt`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yushengsu/lora-diff-Kimi-K2.5/blob/main/compare_sample_train_data.pt), request `max_new_tokens=0`, return input-token logprobs, and compare 1808 positions.

Dataset input-logprob diff:

| Pair | mean abs | max abs | half squared mean | identical |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A vs B | 0.101421 | 3.921772 | 0.065445 | false |
| B vs PR2 C-nolora | 0.102540 | 3.790158 | 0.053243 | false |
| B vs PR3 C-nolora | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | 0.000000 | true |
| PR2 C-lora vs PR3 C-lora | 0.232877 | 2.967687 | 0.080574 | false |

This is the accuracy slice: the no-LoRA request on the LoRA-enabled unfused runner becomes bit-identical to the fused Cutlass baseline on this 1808-position capture. When rerunning this stacked branch, I rebuilt `sgl-kernel` for PR3 and touched `prepare_moe_input.cu` before the incremental build so Ninja actually recompiled the fp32-factor kernel.

`bs=32`, `input_len=1024`, `output_len=2048`.

| Variant | prefill time (s) | prefill tok/s | decode time (s) | decode tok/s | total latency (s) | overall tok/s |

| PR3 C-lora | 1.72 | 19080 | 411.27 | 159.35 | 412.99 | 238.03 |

The fp32-factor combine improves accuracy and did not introduce a measured perf regression at this shape.
